title: A Bronx busway converts a safety and delay problem into operating access for 39,000 daily riders without yet proving realized time savings
source_unit: NYC Mayor's Office and NYC DOT completion announcement for the Tremont Avenue busway
geography: Tremont Avenue, Bronx, New York City

observations.period: September 23, 2026; Tremont Avenue busway completion and activation

denominator.unit: daily Bx36 riders identified by NYC as served by the corridor

historical_bus_speed.unit: miles per hour, a reported historical low for buses on the corridor

operating_schedule.value: Busway operating seven days a week from 6 a.m. to 8 p.m.

car_ownership_context.unit: percent of households in the transit-dependent community reported as not owning a private car

realized_time_savings.unit: missing post-activation travel times, reliability, missed-connection, fare, accessibility, and rider-level burden measures

mechanism.value: Dedicated busway space and parking deterrence are intended to convert street redesign into faster, more reliable, and safer bus access for a transit-dependent corridor

observations.method: Structured extraction from the official NYC completion announcement; rider denominator, historical speed, operating schedule, car-ownership context, and realized rider outcomes are kept separate.
observations.uncertainty: The announcement does not publish post-activation speed, on-time performance, rider survey, collision, enforcement, displacement, business, noise, or accessibility outcomes. The 39,000 figure is a daily service population, not a panel of observed riders.
observations.subgroup: Daily Bx36 riders and households along a transit-dependent Bronx corridor; no rider-level income, disability, race, age, work, or school outcome is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: A busway can protect transit capacity and reduce parking interference while shifting curb access, traffic, enforcement, noise, or delivery burdens to adjacent streets; intended faster service is not measured rider benefit.

related_sources.claim: The August construction announcement describes the planned operating hours and the busway's intended time and safety mechanism.
NYC DOT and MTA describe the broader Fast Buses, Better Service program and its citywide implementation context.

boundary: This record establishes a completed and activated Bronx busway serving a named daily rider population in a transit-dependent corridor. It does not establish realized time savings, reliability, safety, accessibility, affordability, adjacent-neighborhood burden, or durable rider legitimacy.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the official NYC Mayor's Office completion-announcement HTML retrieved for extraction.
